hook: Two runners' speed graphs weave over and under each other during a race. The space between the graphs on a stretch where one runner is faster is real area, and so is the space where the other is faster. One integral would let those pieces cancel; to count all of the area, you have to cut the integral where the graphs cross.

prereq.q: If $\int_0^2 h(x)\,dx = 5$ and $\int_2^6 h(x)\,dx = -3$, what is $\int_0^6 h(x)\,dx$?
The line $y = x + 1$ is above the parabola $y = x^2 - 1$ between their crossings. What is the height of a vertical strip between them?

figure.caption: Where $f(x) = x^3 - 3x$ and $g(x) = x$ cross, top and bottom swap. The two pieces have area 4 each, but one integral of $f - g$ from $-2$ to $2$ gives 0.

chain.cause: Two graphs cross inside the interval
chain.effect: the curve on top changes at each crossing
one integral of $f - g$ counts that piece as negative and cancels area

chain.cause: Split the integral at every crossing and use top minus bottom on each piece
chain.effect: every piece is positive, and their sum is the area

chain.cause: Top minus bottom on each piece is $|f(x) - g(x)|$
chain.effect: the area is also $\int_a^b |f(x) - g(x)|\,dx$, which a calculator can evaluate in one step

ideas: Splitting the integral: find every crossing inside the interval by solving $f(x) = g(x)$, then integrate top minus bottom on each piece and add.
One integral $\int_a^b (f - g)\,dx$ is a net value: areas where $g$ is on top are subtracted.
Area $= \int_a^b |f(x) - g(x)|\,dx$. On a calculator, this is the fastest setup.
Crossings outside the interval do not create pieces, and the interval's ends are not crossings.
The same rule holds in $y$: split where the right and left edges swap.

misconception.wrong: If the integral of $f - g$ comes out negative or zero, take its absolute value to get the area.
misconception.right: By the time you take the absolute value, the pieces have already cancelled. Split at each crossing first (or put the absolute value inside the integral), then add the positive pieces.

summary: When curves cross more than twice, top and bottom swap at each crossing. Find the crossings, split the integral there, use top minus bottom on each piece, and add: the area is $\int_a^b |f(x) - g(x)|\,dx$. A single integral of $f - g$ gives a net amount, not the area.
